answer.rationale: With only 14 days before the primary contract lapses and the line already at 94% of committed volume with zero buffer, any move that introduces onboarding or integration uncertainty (switching vendors, adding a second source) carries outsized delivery risk right now. memory_c2's cost win from switching vendors is a single data point without confirmation of how it would perform under this tight timeline and lack of slack, so it shouldn't be relied on for an irreversible switch this cycle. memory_c4 indicates that renegotiating at renewal with market benchmarking can recover real margin while keeping the same supply relationship intact, which directly supports the finance mandate for cost reduction without disturbing the stable, low-risk delivery pattern seen in memory_c1. Verifying c4's original record lets me confirm the actual magnitude and terms of that past renegotiation before committing spend-reduction expectations to it. Negotiating terms with the incumbent ahead of the 14-day expiry addresses the cost mandate while preserving delivery continuity, and defers the higher-risk structural changes (vendor switch, second sourcing) to the next review cycle when there's more time to de-risk onboarding.
